name: Spaghetti bolognese
summary: A rich beef mince and tomato sauce, slow-simmered with onion, carrot and garlic, tossed with spaghetti and finished with grated cheese.
about: Spaghetti bolognese is one of the most-cooked family dinners in South Africa. Local homes make it with beef mince, plenty of tomato and grated carrot, and serve it with grated cheddar. It stretches a packet of mince, children love it, and the sauce freezes well.
steps: Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat. Add the mince and fry for 8–10 minutes, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, until all the pink is gone and it starts to brown.
Turn the heat to medium, add the onions and carrots and cook, stirring, for 6–8 minutes until the onions are soft and translucent. Stir in the garlic and herbs for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, then add the tomatoes, stock, sugar, bay leaf, salt and pepper. Bring to the boil.

Turn the heat to low, half-cover the pot and simmer for 40 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until the sauce is thick and rich and the oil starts to pool at the edges. Add a splash of water if it catches. Taste for salt and remove the bay leaf.

About 15 minutes before the sauce is ready, bring a large pot of well-salted water to a rolling boil. Cook the spaghetti for the time on the packet, usually 9–11 minutes, until tender but still with a little bite, then drain.
Serve the spaghetti in bowls with the sauce spooned over, topped with grated cheddar.
prepNote: The sauce keeps 3 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen; cook the spaghetti fresh.
